task.description: Write test spec and test code for REQ-031 (Letflow.Definitions.ServiceScopeValidator, SVC-03), whose implementation just PASSed SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) and REVIEWER (Step 2d). Scope test: real application-executable surface exists (lib/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator.ex, 353 lines, pure functional code) -- full WF-02 Step 3 procedure applies, not the docs-only skip path. Cover all 5 acceptance criteria plus the additional coverage the design/review process specifically flagged: both deliberate R-Co asymmetries (INV-SSV-5, INV-SSV-9) as their own named test cases, first-violation-wins/short-circuit semantics proven via raise-if-called-again lookups, malformed/garbage lookup results failing closed (SECURITY-REVIEWER OQ-1), and skip behavior for nodes with no service_id/plugin_handler attribute and non-SERVICE_TASK nodes. AC4 (activate/2 hook wiring) requires a real-Postgres integration test against the real, already-merged Letflow.Definitions.activate/2 per DIRECTIVE T-1 -- no mocking.
acceptance_criteria: test/specs/REQ-031.md written, mapping every AC + the flagged extra coverage to concrete test cases with a 'why this exists' rationale, not a restatement of the criterion

Test code under test/letflow/ following existing project conventions (pure-function unit tests mirroring graph_test.exs's shape; DB-backed integration test mirroring store_test.exs's provisioned_tenant/1 pattern)
Every acceptance criterion has >=1 test case that would fail if violated
Both R-Co asymmetries (INV-SSV-5 plugin-not-registered-passes, INV-SSV-9 plugin-nil-owner-passes) get their own named test cases, not incidental coverage
Short-circuit (Enum.reduce_while/3) proven via a lookup that raises if called a second time, not merely asserted on the returned violation
Malformed lookup results confirmed to fail closed (raise), both service and plugin sides independently
AC4 uses the real, merged Letflow.Definitions.activate/2 and the real ServiceScopeValidator.build/1 output as the hook, against a real Postgres-backed tenant fixture -- no mocked DB or mocked HTTP
No test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness
mix test run on the new files and the full suite, with real quoted output

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-031.md mapping all 5 acceptance criteria plus 5 categories of additionally-flagged coverage (both R-Co asymmetries, first-violation-wins/short-circuit, malformed-lookup fail-closed, skipped-node cases) to concrete, named test cases with rationale for each. Wrote test/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator_test.exs (new file, 24 tests, async: true, no Letflow.Repo/Sandbox anywhere -- mirrors graph_test.exs's pure-module shape) covering AC1 (global-scope passes for any tenant, 2 tests), AC2 (tenant-scoped owner mismatch fails naming node_id+ref_id, plus the necessary positive owning-tenant control, 2 tests), AC3 (not-registered vs owned-elsewhere are distinct, comparable atoms -- not just different strings, 2 tests), AC5 (moduledoc names ServiceCatalog/S6 and PluginRegistry/S3 and states neither is implemented today, 3 tests, own local normalized_moduledoc/1 helper matching the pattern independently established in definitions_test.exs and promotion_review_test.exs -- each file defines its own copy, confirmed by direct comparison), both asymmetries (INV-SSV-5 plugin-not-registered-passes proven by direct contrast against the service side in the same test, and INV-SSV-9 plugin-nil-owner-passes proven as the exact inverse of the service side's INV-SSV-7 violation, 2+2=4 tests, the CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR-rework-triggering decision per this run's history), the plugin mismatched-owner violation row not otherwise exercised (1 test), first-violation-wins proven via a :counters-backed lookup that raises if called a second time (cross-node) and a plugin_lookup that raises if called at all (within-node, proving the with-chain halts at the service check before reaching the plugin check on the same node) (2 tests), malformed lookup results (an out-of-contract atom neither {:ok,_} nor {:error, :not_registered}) proven to raise FunctionClauseError rather than silently pass, independently for both service_lookup and plugin_lookup (2 tests), skipped-node cases (attributes: nil, attributes present but missing both keys, empty-string/non-string/missing service_id, and a non-SERVICE_TASK node carrying a service_id-shaped attribute) all proven via a raise-if-called Lookup so a passing test is a genuine proof of skip, not a coincidental pass (4 tests), and build/1's own forwarding contract (2 tests). Extended test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs with a new 'activate/2 (REQ-031 AC4)' describe block (3 tests) and a new graph_with_service_task/1 fixture (a real, validate_graph/1-and-validate_node_attributes/1-passing graph carrying a SERVICE_TASK node with endpoint/timeout_ms/service_id attributes, confirmed against graph.ex's CHK-10/CHK-11 requirements by direct reading) -- this reuses store_test.exs's existing real-Postgres provisioned_tenant/1/create!/2/reread!/2/count_active_by_name/2 fixtures (DIRECTIVE T-1, no mocked DB) rather than duplicating tenant-provisioning machinery in a new file, consistent with how REQ-030's own activate/2 hook-mechanism tests are already organized in this same file. The 3 new tests demonstrate: (1) a Lookup causing a violation, wired via the real ServiceScopeValidator.build/1 (not a hand-rolled closure, unlike REQ-030's own AC6 tests which pre-date this module), blocks activation with the real, full Violation struct surfacing unchanged through activate/2's {:error, {:service_scope_violation, violation}} wrap, definition stays :draft, zero rows ACTIVE; (2) the identical graph/service_id (which WOULD fail if the hook ran) activates successfully when the :service_scope_validator key is omitted entirely -- proving the nil-skip path is a genuine skip, not an accidentally-permissive default, per the design doc's own 'demonstration shape for TEST-DESIGNER' note (design doc section 6), executed literally; (3) a permitting Lookup wired the same way lets activation succeed, closing the gap a suite containing only the blocking case would leave. Ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean) and mix format --check-formatted (failed once on the newly-added code's line lengths/nesting, fixed via mix format on the two touched files, re-verified clean). Confirmed baseline before starting: mix test on main-equivalent working tree (before any new test files) returned exactly 570 passed (4 properties, 566 tests), matching the stated baseline. After adding the new test files: mix test test/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs returned 54 passed (all new/extended tests, zero failures) in an isolated run; mix test test/letflow/definitions/service_scope_validator_test.exs test/letflow/definitions/store_test.exs test/letflow/definitions_test.exs returned 67 passed after the format fix (isolated re-run, confirming the format-only changes did not alter behavior); full mix test (whole suite, twice, before and after the format fix) returned 597 passed (4 properties, 593 tests) both times -- exactly 570+27 (24 new pure tests + 3 new integration tests), zero pre-existing tests broken, zero regressions.
